### Oklahoma City

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-04-21
- **Normalized date:** `2026-04-21` (exact)
- **Duration:** Until 2026-12-31, or earlier if data center zoning amendments are adopted
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ok-oklahoma-city-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Emergency ordinance introduced and adopted unanimously by City Council on 2026-04-21 as Council Agenda Item XI.U; amended 2026-05-19 by a 7-2 Council vote to add a 75 MW threshold and named facility exemptions. The assigned ordinance number(s) could not be confirmed via a primary source actually accessed in this pass — direct attempts to reach library.municode.com/ok/oklahoma_city and okc.gov's ordinance PDF both returned HTTP 403 [VERIFY assigned ordinance number(s) from the Office of the City Clerk for both the original 2026-04-21 ordinance and the 2026-05-19 amendment]
- **What prompted it:** First large data center rezoning requests; no specific zoning use unit or regulations for data centers; concerns about water, electricity, noise, infrastructure, and other public impacts
- **Affected projects:** New applications for rezoning requests and permits, including building permits, for data center construction, expansion, or use; two pending rezoning requests are exempted
- **Detailed status:** Active, as amended. On 2026-05-19, City Council voted 7-2 to amend the moratorium to allow data centers using up to 75 megawatts of electricity to apply for zoning and construction permits, and carved out two named exemptions: the Scale Datacenters facility on the Expand Energy (formerly Chesapeake) campus (serving Cerebras AI), and the Rack59 Data Center at 7725 W. Reno Ave. As of the most recent reporting reviewed (dated 2026-06-25), no comprehensive data-center zoning use-unit had been adopted, so the underlying moratorium (through 2026-12-31 or earlier zoning adoption) remains in force. No source dated in July 2026 was located to independently confirm currency as of 2026-07-31.
- **Outcome:** City is using the pause to evaluate impacts and draft zoning code amendments for data centers
